nodes.label: SUPER_ADMIN Role
nodes.rationale: Full platform + access control; granted the wildcard '*' so it always has every permission code regardless of matrix edits.

nodes.label: ADMIN Role
nodes.rationale: Store operations role covering overview, orders, products, categories, customers, queries, and reviews — deliberately excludes devices/access so operational staff cannot see device telemetry or RBAC controls.

nodes.label: STAFF Role
nodes.rationale: Day-to-day operations role, identical to ADMIN's default grant set minus reviews.manage — reviews moderation is reserved for a more trusted tier.

nodes.label: CacheInterceptor
nodes.rationale: Registered after EncryptInterceptor in AppModule's APP_INTERCEPTOR list so that, given Nest's first-registered-first pipe order, encryption wraps both cache hits and misses on the wire while the cache itself stores only plain ResponseVm.

nodes.label: EncryptInterceptor
nodes.rationale: Registered before CacheInterceptor so every response, whether served from cache or freshly computed, is encrypted on the wire when ENABLE_ENCRYPTION is on.

nodes.label: ClientDevice Tracking
nodes.rationale: DB upsert is debounced to 5 minutes to avoid write amplification from high-traffic fingerprints, except when a request is rate-limited, in which case the block is recorded immediately so blockedCount stays accurate.

nodes.label: CUSTOMER Role
nodes.rationale: Represents storefront shoppers (non-staff); documented as having no admin access, distinguishing it from the three staff roles that are actually seeded via permissions.yml role_defaults.

nodes.label: Module-Driven Route/Cache/Security Config Pattern
nodes.rationale: Each domain module owns a config/module.yml declaring its routes, auth requirements, cache TTLs, and security settings (encryption, rate limits) so cross-cutting guards/interceptors (RateLimitGuard, CacheInterceptor) can behave generically by reading module config instead of hardcoding per-module logic.

nodes.label: Sealed Session Cookie Design
nodes.rationale: Admin session cookie rc_admin_token is AES-GCM sealed rather than a raw JWT so that DevTools no longer exposes JWT claims directly; AuthGuard unseals the cookie via openToken before verifying the JWT payload.
